pages.title: Controls
pages.description: Every visible thing on screen is a control. In Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) a control is the return value of a factory like TextBlock(...) or Button(...) — a plain element you compose, chain modifiers onto, and return from Render().

pages.title: Charting
pages.description: ReactorD3 brings data visualization to Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor). The chart DSL provides high-level LineChart, BarChart, AreaChart, and PieChart factories that produce standard Reactor elements. You bind data, configure appearance with a fluent API, and the chart renders as native WinUI shapes on a Canvas.

pages.title: Collections
pages.description: When you need to render a list of data, Reactor provides three typed collection elements and a simple ForEach helper.

pages.title: Data System
pages.description: Reactor's data system provides a virtualized DataGrid<T> backed by a pluggable data source abstraction. You define columns (or auto-generate them), connect a data source, and the grid handles sorting, filtering, searching, selection, and inline editing.

pages.title: Dialogs and Flyouts
pages.description: ContentDialog, MenuFlyout, CommandBarFlyout and Popup: when to reach for each one, and how to drive them from component state.

pages.title: Forms and Input
pages.description: Every form control in Reactor follows the controlled-input pattern: you own the value, you provide the change handler, and the control reflects your state. There is no two-way binding. The data always flows one direction.

pages.title: Status and Info
pages.description: Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor)'s status and info controls report what the app is doing without stealing focus. Reach for them when the user needs to know something — a save succeeded, a long operation is running, a feature exists — and doesn't need to decide anything.

pages.title: Text and Media
pages.description: This page covers display text, inline rich text, rich-text editing, and media controls in Reactor.

pages.title: Win2D canvas
pages.description: Reactor.Advanced exposes the three Win2D canvas controls as Reactor elements. Add the package when you need immediate-mode drawing.

pages.title: Reactor
pages.description: Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) is a declarative UI framework for building native Windows desktop apps in pure C#. No XAML. No data binding. No view models. You describe your UI as a function of state, and Reactor keeps the screen in sync.

pages.title: Cheat Sheet
pages.description: Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) at a glance. Every row links to the page that covers it in depth.

pages.title: Getting Started with Reactor
pages.description: Install Reactor, scaffold a project, and grow it from hello world to a todo list and a calculator.

pages.title: Reactor vs XAML
pages.description: This page is for the XAML developer who wants the why behind Reactor's design.

pages.title: Rules of Reactor
pages.description: Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor)'s render loop has a small set of invariants. Most are enforced by analyzers, so a violation surfaces at build time with a specific code; the rest are conventions that the framework expects. This page lists them, names the analyzer where one exists, and shows the before/after pair so the catch is visible.

pages.title: Thinking in Reactor
pages.description: Coming soon — this page is the mental-model essay that frames Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) for new readers: UI as a function of state, why there is no XAML, when to reach for hooks, and how components compose.

pages.title: Reactor for XAML Developers
pages.description: If you already know XAML, Reactor is not a different Windows UI stack. It still renders real WinUI controls. The shift is in how you describe the UI: instead of splitting a page across XAML, bindings, converters, and code-behind, you return the UI directly from C# and let Reactor keep the native control tree in sync.

pages.title: Accessibility
pages.description: Reactor provides accessibility modifiers on every component. They map directly to WinUI's automation properties, so screen readers, keyboard navigation, and test tools work out of the box.

pages.title: Advanced Patterns
pages.description: Escape hatches for the few jobs the declarative model doesn't fit: error boundaries, memoized subtrees, element refs, direct property writes, view-model bridges, and custom hooks.

pages.title: Animation
pages.description: Reactor animations are declarative. You set the target value (opacity, scale, translation) and attach a transition modifier.

pages.title: Async Resources
pages.description: Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor)'s async hooks — UseResource, UseInfiniteResource, and UseMutation — replace the "one UseState for data, one for loading, one for error, one UseEffect to tie them together" pattern. They own the fetch lifecycle: cancellation on deps-change, drop late results after unmount, shared caching across siblings, and stale-while-revalidate by default.

pages.title: Commanding
pages.description: A Command bundles an action with its metadata. Define it once and use it across buttons, menus, toolbars, and dialogs — the metadata stays consistent everywhere.

pages.title: Components
pages.description: Components are the building blocks of a Reactor app. Each component is a class with a Render() method that returns an element tree describing its UI.

pages.title: Context
pages.description: Context lets you pass data through the component tree without threading it through every level of props. Define a Context<T>, provide a value at any level, and any descendant can read it with UseContext.

pages.title: Dev Tooling
pages.description: Reactor's inner loop centers on dotnet watch and preview mode: you edit code, save, and see changes in a running window — no manual restart, no state-resetting class reload most of the time.

pages.title: Diagnostics
pages.description: This page is about reading Reactor's diagnostics from a real app — not about adding new events.

pages.title: Docking Windows
pages.description: Microsoft.UI.Reactor's docking system lets a single shell host multiple user-rearrangeable surfaces — the Visual Studio / VS Code / Photoshop / Figma layout idiom. Users drag tabs between groups, split panes, pin tool windows to a side, and tear panes out into floating sub-windows; layouts persist across sessions.

pages.title: Effects and Lifecycle
pages.description: UseEffect runs side effects — code that reaches outside the component's render function. Timers, data fetching, subscriptions, and DOM manipulation all belong in effects, not in Render().

pages.title: Flex Layout
pages.description: FlexPanel is a Yoga-backed CSS Flexbox implementation, exposed through the FlexRow and FlexColumn factories. Reach for it when the layout needs alignment control, wrapping, or proportional sizing that VStack and HStack cannot express.

pages.title: Hooks
pages.description: Hooks are functions you call inside Render() to manage state, side effects, and memoization. They replace the need for view models, event handlers, and lifecycle methods.

pages.title: Input and gestures
pages.description: Reactor's input surface is declarative: attach handlers via .On* modifiers and the reconciler wires WinUI events, auto-enables the matching flags (for example IsDoubleTapEnabled), and survives re-renders without re-subscribing the underlying WinUI event.

pages.title: Layout
pages.description: Reactor provides a small set of layout primitives that compose to build any screen structure. Every layout element accepts children and optional spacing.

pages.title: Localization
pages.description: Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor)'s localization system wraps your component tree in a LocaleProvider that supplies an IntlAccessor to every descendant via context. You look up messages, format numbers and dates, and detect RTL layouts — all locale-aware, all reactive.

pages.title: Navigation
pages.description: Reactor uses a stack-based navigation model with type-safe routes. You define your routes as an enum, create a navigation handle with UseNavigation, and render the current page with NavigationHost.

pages.title: Migration: Optional<T> controlled props
pages.description: Spec 050 changes controlled element-record properties from plain T to Optional<T>. Factory calls such as TextBox(text, setText), Slider(value, 0, 100, setValue), and ComboBox(items, index, setIndex) keep their existing plain-value signatures; they wrap the value in Optional<T>.Of(value) internally. Most app code therefore keeps compiling unchanged.

pages.title: Packaging
pages.description: A Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) app is a normal WinUI 3 / Windows App SDK executable — dotnet publish produces the deployable artifact and the framework itself adds nothing exotic to the project file.

pages.title: Performance
pages.description: A top-down performance workflow: take a trace with dotnet-trace or PerfView, learn what each span means, find the outlier, and reproduce a benchmark so a regression has a number behind it.

pages.title: Persistence
pages.description: UsePersisted holds a value past a component re-mount — the user navigates away, the component unmounts, the user navigates back, and the captured state is still there.

pages.title: Styling and Theming
pages.description: Color and style your UI with theme tokens, named-style modifiers, and resource overrides that follow the Light, Dark, and high-contrast themes automatically.

pages.title: Testing
pages.description: Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor)'s render loop is deterministic and synchronous. A Component mounted in a unit test renders, runs effects, accepts state updates, re-renders, and disposes through the same code path the WinUI host uses — minus the WinUI tree at the bottom.

pages.title: Theming Tokens
pages.description: Reactor exposes 36 named theme tokens on the static Theme class plus a Theme.Ref(string) escape hatch for any XAML resource key.

pages.title: Visual Studio Embedded Preview
pages.description: The Visual Studio Embedded Preview hosts a live Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) component inside a Visual Studio tool window — Visual Studio 2026 (18.x), with the Visual Studio extension development workload. Unlike the VS Code preview, which streams screenshots, the Visual Studio extension embeds the real WinUI surface so mouse, keyboard, focus, popups, and accessibility tree inspection work against the running app.

pages.title: Advanced Windowing
pages.description: Some shell-window ideas are possible on Windows only by leaving the safe Reactor contract. We document the recipe so expert apps can make an informed choice, but Reactor does not ship these primitives as first-class WindowSpec fields.

pages.title: Migration: Windowing evolution
pages.description: Spec 054 intentionally removes a few legacy windowing fields in favor of more explicit shapes. The new APIs are additive except for the breaking changes below.

pages.title: Windows
pages.description: Most Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) apps start with the single window created by ReactorApp.Run. Larger desktop apps can open multiple native WinUI top-level windows with WindowSpec and ReactorApp.OpenWindow, while keeping the same declarative component model used inside a page.

pages.title: WinForms Interop
pages.description: Reactor components can run inside WinForms applications using XAML Islands. The Reactor.Interop.WinForms package provides XamlIslandControl — a standard WinForms control that hosts a Reactor component tree with full keyboard, accessibility, and theming support.

pages.title: WPF Interop
pages.description: Host Reactor components inside a WPF app with a XAML island, until a first-class WPF host control ships.

pages.title: Analyzer Architecture
pages.description: This page walks through the Reactor analyzer pipeline end-to-end: how a diagnostic descriptor wires into the C# compilation, what happens on each InvocationExpression, and how to add your own rule.

pages.title: Animation Pipeline
pages.description: This page maps the four authoring surfaces onto the underlying compositor and explains the trade-offs that pick one surface over another.

pages.title: Architecture Overview
pages.description: This page maps Reactor's runtime end-to-end so the rest of the Under-the-hood track has a shared diagram to point at.

pages.title: The Control Reconciler Protocol
pages.description: This page documents the data path between the reconciler and the WinUI control it edits. It is for anyone extending Reactor with a new native control, or debugging why an existing element does not update the way it should.

pages.title: DevTools Internals
pages.description: This page covers the internals of Reactor's devtools — the MCP server that external agents talk to, the in-app dev menu, the runtime overlays, and the gate that keeps the whole subsystem out of retail.

pages.title: Effects Scheduling
pages.description: This page is about when UseEffect fires and why.

pages.title: Element Pool
pages.description: The Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) element pool recycles unmounted WinUI controls so a scroll-heavy list or fast-mounting subtree doesn't allocate a fresh TextBlock / Button / Border on every render.

pages.title: Extending Reactor with Native Controls
pages.description: How to wrap a native Windows control as a Reactor element — a third-party WinUI control, a custom Control subclass, or an existing WinUI control that the built-in catalog has not yet covered.

pages.title: Focus and Input Internals
pages.description: This page covers the input subsystem from the routed-event boundary through the Reactor hooks that observe it.

pages.title: Hooks Internals
pages.description: One description of the storage shape behind every hook — enough to debug a HookOrderException, predict whether UseState returns a stable setter, and know when reaching for UseRef is correct.

pages.title: Modifier System
pages.description: This page is the runtime view of the same fluent chain that Styling introduces from the surface.

pages.title: Perf Instrumentation
pages.description: This page covers what Reactor publishes, where to read it, and how to get a clean trace.

pages.title: Reactivity Model
pages.description: This page is the why behind the hooks surface. If you've come from XAML and INotifyPropertyChanged, the change of model is larger than the syntax.

pages.title: Reconciliation
pages.description: This page absorbs the legacy docs/reference/reconciliation.md. The goal is one place to learn how Reactor diffs trees — the same information, in the structure the rest of the guide uses, plus the source pointers that let you verify it.

pages.title: Source Mapping
pages.description: "Source mapping" in Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) is the chain that ties a runtime artifact — an ETW event, a --preview overlay highlight, a thrown exception — back to the C# source that produced it.

pages.title: Threading and Dispatch
pages.description: Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) has one UI thread invariant: the reconciler, every hook setter, and every WinUI property write must happen on the thread that captured the dispatcher at app bootstrap.

pages.title: Recipes
pages.description: A recipe is a small composition of Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) primitives that solves a real UI problem — login, master-detail, settings, paginated list, modal confirmation, multi-step form, search-with-suggestions, command palette, drag-to-reorder. The recipes here are not exhaustive apps; each is a single screen showing the pattern, and each ships a tiny doc app you can clone and adapt.

pages.title: Recipe: Command Palette
pages.description: A command palette is a filter-as-you-type list with a keyboard accelerator to open and Enter to execute. In Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) it's three UseState hooks, a static catalog of Command records, and an OnPreviewKeyDown handler — no menubar, no modal manager, no view model.

pages.title: Recipe: Drag to Reorder
pages.description: Drag-reorder is a UseState<List<T>> plus a function that splices one item from one index to another. Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor)'s keyed reconciler does the rest — moves preserve identity, so the same row element keeps its focus, its hover state, and its place in the visual tree. Pointer drag is one entry point; an Alt+Up / Alt+Down keyboard shortcut is the second, and it carries the accessibility story.

pages.title: Recipe: Login
pages.description: A Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) login form is four pieces working together: validated input, submit-gated state, an async call, and an error-display surface. The recipe below wires them with two UseState hooks and one UseMutation — no view model, no event handler classes, and no hand-rolled submitting / error flags.

pages.title: Recipe: Master-detail
pages.description: Master-detail in Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) is the canonical multi-pane shape: a list of records on one side, the selected record's details on the other. The whole thing is one UseState for the selected id and two slots in an HStack.

pages.title: Recipe: Modal dialog
pages.description: The modal is an element you return conditionally. There is no special "open dialog" API — when open is true the tree includes the modal panel layered over the page; when it's false the modal element is absent and the page renders alone.

pages.title: Recipe: Multi-Step Form
pages.description: A wizard form is a step-index UseState plus a switch on which step renders. The field state lives in the same component as the step index, so moving forward and back never loses what the user typed — Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) doesn't unmount the surrounding component when the visible slot changes.

pages.title: Recipe: Paginated List
pages.description: A paginated list is four states sharing one source of truth: an initial load, a populated list, a "load the next page" affordance, and a terminal "no more results." UseInfiniteResource owns all four in Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) — the component below pattern-matches on LoadState and reads Items directly; there is no local UseState for loading or errors.

pages.title: Recipe: Search with suggestions
pages.description: The pattern is two slots: an input that owns the query string, and a dropdown that shows zero or more suggestions filtered against a catalog. UseMemo keys the filter on the query, so a re-render that didn't touch the query is free — important for the keyboard-up- arrow-down-arrow loop where the suggestion index changes but the query doesn't.

pages.title: Recipe: Settings page
pages.description: A settings page is many small persisted prefs side-by-side. Each preference is its own UsePersisted call with its own key — there's no central settings object that needs migration when one preference moves. The row layout is a single helper.

pages.title: Hooks reference
pages.description: Hooks are how Reactor components subscribe to state, schedule effects, and reach into the framework's lifecycle from a function-shaped Render body. Each entry on this index is generated from the <summary> XML doc comments authored alongside the source in src/Reactor/Hooks/ — the canonical surface — and is grouped by the hooks category in docs/_pipeline/reference-map.yaml.

pages.title: AnnounceRegionElement
pages.description: Internal Reactor element that mounts a hidden TextBlock with LiveSetting for announcements.

pages.title: AnyLoading
pages.description: True iff any tracked token is currently Loading.

pages.title: CacheKey
pages.description: Overrides the generated cache key; null uses a key derived from deps. When set, the key identifies the query; deps changes alone do not cancel an in-flight request or start a new fetch. Include values that select different data in the key, for example $"user:{userId}".

pages.title: CacheTime
pages.description: Retention after the last subscriber leaves; null uses five minutes.

pages.title: Changed
pages.description: Fires when a resource joins, leaves, or changes its loading state.

pages.title: Clear
pages.description: Clears all registrations.

pages.title: Count
pages.description: Snapshot the number of registered tokens (loading or not). Diagnostic only.

pages.title: CursorFromPageIndex
pages.description: Optional: computes the cursor for an arbitrary page index directly, bypassing the "wait for page N-1" constraint. Used by UseDataSource to expose the offset semantics of IDataSource's ContinuationToken, so deep scrolls fetch pages in parallel instead of walking the chain one round-trip at a time.

pages.title: Customize
pages.description: Author hook — add the bespoke descriptor entries for the [WrapManual] props.

pages.title: Fields
pages.description: Registered field names in order.

pages.title: FocusAttached
pages.description: Attached metadata for focus registration on elements.

pages.title: FocusExtensions
pages.description: Fluent extensions for attaching focus management to elements. Uses .Set() to capture the WinUI control reference during mount/update.

pages.title: FocusField
pages.description: Focuses a specific field by name.

pages.title: FocusFirst
pages.description: Focuses the first field from the given list that exists in this manager. Useful with ValidationContext.InvalidFields.

pages.title: FocusManager
pages.description: Manages focus for a set of registered form fields. Supports programmatic focus control, enter-to-advance, and field ordering.

pages.title: FocusMeta
pages.description: Registers any element with a FocusManager via attached metadata (for custom types).

pages.title: FocusNext
pages.description: Focuses the field after the given field in registration order. If the current field is the last one, triggers submit.

pages.title: FocusPrevious
pages.description: Focuses the field before the given field in registration order.

pages.title: FocusTrap
pages.description: Attaches a focus trap to this element. When the trap is active, Tab/Shift+Tab cycles within this element's visual subtree.

pages.title: FocusTrapElementExtensions
pages.description: Fluent extension to attach a FocusTrapHandle to an element. The handle captures the mounted WinUI element for focus trapping.

pages.title: FocusTrapHandle
pages.description: Handle returned by UseFocusTrap. When active, traps keyboard focus within the container element so Tab/Shift+Tab cycles within the trapped scope. Essential for modal dialogs and flyouts.

pages.title: GetFocus
pages.description: Gets the FocusAttached metadata from an element.

pages.title: IHookDispatcher
pages.description: Abstraction for marshalling continuations back to the render thread. Null-safe — if the callback is absent the continuation runs inline on the thread-pool completion thread (tests and headless hosts).

pages.title: InfiniteHookState
pages.description: Per-hook state for UseInfiniteResource. Coordinates in-flight page fetches, cache subscriptions, deps-change restart, and unmount teardown.

pages.title: IsActive
pages.description: Whether the focus trap is currently active.

pages.title: IsFirstField
pages.description: Returns true if the given field is the first registered field.

pages.title: IsLastField
pages.description: Returns true if the given field is the last registered field.

pages.title: LastResult
pages.description: Most recent successful result, or default if none yet.

pages.title: MutationHookState
pages.description: Mutable state backing a single UseMutation hook instance. Owned per-component, per-hook-slot; disposed on unmount.

pages.title: NotifyPending
pages.description: Called from RequestPage / page-completion paths to keep the Pending scope in sync.

pages.title: PendingFactory
pages.description: Entry-point factory for the Pending bubble-up element. See docs/specs/020-async-resources-design.md §10 for the full mechanism.

pages.title: PendingScope
pages.description: Shared loading-state ref-count consumed by the Pending element and populated by UseResource / UseInfiniteResource hooks inside the scope. When the scope observes any registered resource in the Loading state (not Reloading), the owning Pending element renders its fallback instead of the child subtree.

pages.title: Post
pages.description: Enqueue action to run on the dispatcher thread.

pages.title: RefetchOnMount
pages.description: Whether to fetch on a cache miss.

pages.title: RefetchOnWindowFocus
pages.description: Whether to opt into window-focus revalidation.

pages.title: Region
pages.description: A zero-size, invisible Reactor element that acts as the live-region anchor. Include this anywhere in your component tree (it renders nothing visible).

pages.title: ResourceHookState
pages.description: Mutable state backing a single UseResource hook instance. Instances are owned per-component, per-hook-slot, and are disposed on unmount.

pages.title: RetryCount
pages.description: Number of retries after a failed fetch.

pages.title: RunAsync
pages.description: Kick off the mutator with input. Returns a task that completes with the mutator's result or fault.

pages.title: SetControl
pages.description: Associates a WinUI control with a field name. Called from .Set() during mount/update.

pages.title: SetLoading
pages.description: Update token's loading state. Silently ignored if the token was never registered (defensive — avoids forcing the caller to track whether they registered).

pages.title: SetSubmitHandler
pages.description: Sets the callback for submit (Enter on last field).

pages.title: StaleTime
pages.description: Freshness interval; null uses zero.

pages.title: Unregister
pages.description: Stop tracking token. Idempotent.

pages.title: UseAnnounceExtensions
pages.description: Extension methods for the UseAnnounce hook.

pages.title: UseClosingGuard
pages.description: Registers a synchronous "can the window close right now?" predicate. Multiple guards stack — any returning false cancels the close. Runs on the UI thread; for async confirmation, return false and re-trigger ReactorWindow.Close from the dialog callback. No-op outside a window. (spec 036 §7 / §13.4)

pages.title: UseCollection
pages.description: Subscribes to an ObservableCollection and re-renders on Add/Remove/Reset. Returns the collection as IReadOnlyList.

pages.title: UseColorScheme
pages.description: Returns the app-global ColorScheme — ColorScheme.Light or ColorScheme.Dark, read from Application.Current.RequestedTheme.

pages.title: UseContext
pages.description: Reads the nearest ancestor's provided value for the given context. Returns the context's DefaultValue if no provider exists in the ancestor chain. Follows hook rules — must be called in the same order every render.

pages.title: UseDevtools
pages.description: Returns true when the current process is running with the in-app devtools UI enabled. This is the AND of two independent signals:

pages.title: UseDisplays
pages.description: Returns the current display snapshot and re-renders when the display layout changes.

pages.title: UseDpi
pages.description: Returns the current per-window DPI (ReactorWindow.Dpi) and re-renders on DPI change. Returns the system primary-monitor DPI when called outside a window. (spec 036 §5.2)

pages.title: UseElementFocusExtensions
pages.description: Hook for imperative element focus (spec 027 Tier 5). Returns a stable ElementRef (survives re-renders) plus a RequestFocus action that schedules Input.FocusManager.Focus on the UI dispatcher. Scheduling defers focus past the current reconcile pass so callers can safely request focus from effects or event handlers without racing against layout.

pages.title: UseElementRefExtensions
pages.description: Hook that returns a strongly-typed ElementRef for binding to a concrete WinUI control via the .Ref(...) modifier. The typed ref removes the (Button)ref.Current cast at consumers (Composition, Ink, focus, …).

pages.title: UseExternalStore
pages.description: Subscribes to an external store that exposes a current snapshot getter. Re-renders only when a change notification yields a different snapshot.

pages.title: UseFocusExtensions
pages.description: Extension methods for the UseFocus hook.

pages.title: UseFocusTrapExtensions
pages.description: Extension methods for the UseFocusTrap hook.

pages.title: UseHighContrast
pages.description: Returns true when the system is in a High Contrast (forced colors) theme. Automatically re-renders the component when high contrast is toggled.

pages.title: UseHighContrastScheme
pages.description: Returns the high contrast scheme name (e.g., "High Contrast Black", "High Contrast White") or null if not in high contrast mode. Automatically re-renders the component when the scheme changes.

pages.title: UseInfiniteResourceExtensions
pages.description: Extension methods providing UseInfiniteResource on RenderContext.

pages.title: UseIntl
pages.description: Returns an IntlAccessor for the current locale. Re-renders this component when the locale changes via a parent LocaleProvider. If no LocaleProvider is present, returns a default accessor using the OS locale. Uses Context internally — the context system handles re-renders automatically.

pages.title: UseIsActive
pages.description: Subscribes to the host window's activation events and re-renders on change. Returns true outside a window (the surface is "active" while shown). (spec 036 §7)

pages.title: UseIsCovered
pages.description: Returns a covered hint from the host window's z-order transitions and re-renders on change. The value is not pixel-accurate occlusion state.

pages.title: UseIsDarkTheme
pages.description: Convenience wrapper — returns true when the app-global color scheme is ColorScheme.Dark. Exactly UseColorScheme() == ColorScheme.Dark, so it inherits that hook's semantics: it does not observe per-element RequestedTheme.

pages.title: UseMemoCellsExtensions
pages.description: Cell-level memoization hook for high-frequency list / grid bodies. Reuses element references for cells whose item value (and declared dependencies) haven't changed since the previous render. The reconciler short-circuits on Object.ReferenceEquals, so reused cells skip diffing entirely.

pages.title: UseMutationExtensions
pages.description: Extension methods providing UseMutation on RenderContext.

pages.title: UseNavigationLifecycle
pages.description: Registers lifecycle callbacks that fire during navigation events.

pages.title: UseObservable
pages.description: Subscribes to an INotifyPropertyChanged source and re-renders when any property changes. Returns the same source object.

pages.title: UseObservableProperty
pages.description: Subscribes to a specific property on an INotifyPropertyChanged source. Re-renders only when that property changes.

pages.title: UseObservableTree
pages.description: Observes an object and all nested INotifyPropertyChanged values reachable through its properties. Re-renders when any property at any depth changes. Automatically subscribes/unsubscribes as property values change.

pages.title: UseOpenWindow
pages.description: Open or reuse a secondary window keyed by key. Renders that pass the same key share the same ReactorWindow; if the spec changes across renders the live window is updated via ReactorWindow.Update. The returned handle is identity-stable across renders so long as the key is stable.

pages.title: UseReducedMotion
pages.description: Returns true when the user or system prefers reduced motion (e.g., Windows "Show animations" is off, or SPI_GETCLIENTAREAANIMATION returns false). Automatically re-renders the component when the preference changes.

pages.title: UseRef
pages.description: Returns a mutable ref object that persists across renders.

pages.title: UseResourceExtensions
pages.description: Extension methods providing UseResource on RenderContext.

pages.title: UseState
pages.description: Declares a piece of state. Returns (currentValue, setter). Must be called in the same order every render (just like React hooks).

pages.title: UseStateSetterByIndex
pages.description: DEBUG ONLY: Directly set a UseState hook value by index and trigger re-render. Used for testing state changes without event handlers.

pages.title: UseSystemBackButton
pages.description: Subscribes to Alt+Left and VirtualKey.GoBack keyboard events on the given window's content to call NavigationHandle.GoBack. Unsubscribes on unmount.

pages.title: UseTrayIcon
pages.description: Open (or reuse-by-TrayIconSpec.Key) a system-tray icon scoped to the calling component. The icon closes automatically on unmount — that's the only difference from ReactorApp.OpenTrayIcon, which is app-scoped and keeps the icon alive until explicit ReactorTrayIcon.Close.

pages.title: UseWindow
pages.description: Resolves the ReactorWindow whose host renders this component — including nested components and virtualized rows realized outside the host's render pass — or null when it has no owning window (tray-flyout content, ReactorHostControl embeds). O(1) field read; no subscription, no re-render trigger. (spec 036 §7 / §7.1)

pages.title: UseWindowAspectRatio
pages.description: Applies a lifetime-bound width/height aspect lock to the owning window. Last mounted hook wins; unmounting restores the previous writer.

pages.title: UseWindowDragMove
pages.description: Returns a stable callback that starts a framework-managed window drag/move loop (cursor polling + AppWindow.Move at ~60Hz until the left mouse button is released).

pages.title: UseWindowPosition
pages.description: Subscribes to the host window's PositionChanged event and re-renders on change. Returns (0, 0) outside a window. (spec 054 §5.5)

pages.title: UseWindowState
pages.description: Subscribes to the host window's StateChanged event and re-renders on change. Returns WindowState.Normal outside a window. (spec 036 §7)
